text:
elaine: Quick sync: we need a concise benchmark narrative for the webinar hero comparing latency vs unit cost. Goal: an engineer-friendly claim + an enterprise cost hook.
raj: Proposed viz: scatter with cost ($/1k tokens) on x and p50 latency (ms) on y, points colored by deployment mode. Add p99 callouts for 2-3 models.
tomas: Overlay SLA bands at 50ms, 200ms, 500ms so customers can see which models hit which buckets. Keep colors accessible.
emily: Copy idea: "Predictable latency, better unit economics. See which models and deployment modes hit your SLA at lower cost." Keep claims conservative and footnote methodology.
oliver: Slide layout: left = hero scatter + SLA bands; right = small panels: tokens/request histogram, batching impact (bars: no-batch vs 64 vs 256), and a one-line methodology.
cassie: Growth ask: include routing rules for CTAs: SMB -> trial calculator, Enterprise -> book Dedicated consult. Also add an interactive calculator for the webinar page (model + batch -> est $/1k + p50/p95).
deploy-bot: export queued: perf-exports/latency_unit_econ/2876543210.csv (ETA 8m)
raj: I'll take the CSV and produce a vega-lite skeleton for designers. Minimal spec so design can wireframe quickly.
emily: Draft three one-liners to A/B test in promo: 1) "Serve fast, pay less: predictable latency at lower unit cost" 2) "Reduce token spend without sacrificing response time" 3) "Latency SLAs + smarter routing = lower cost per token"
tomas: Methodology footnote: sample size, sequence length quantiles (p10/p50/p90), batching configs, quantization level. Visible but small.
elaine: Assignments: Raj = charts + data table; Oliver = slide mock; Emily = copy + CTA pages; Cassie = CTA routing; Tomas = batching micro-viz. I'll finalize narrative and approve.
raj: Will post first draft chart here in ~3h after export completes.
deploy-bot: perf-exports/latency_unit_econ/2876543210.csv ready (https://files.redwood.test/perf-exports/latency_unit_econ/2876543210.csv)
elaine: Awesome. Post chart and the final chosen headline here for quick review before design handoff. :rocket:
